summary:
AgroNova is an AI farm companion that turns NASA Earth observation data into one clear crop decision for smallholder farmers. A farmer picks a field on a map, and AgroNova reads NASA POWER climate data alongside SMAP soil moisture, GPM rainfall, MODIS vegetation and FIRMS fire detection. Its Rotation Lab then ranks climate-resilient crop plans using deterministic scoring and Liebig’s Law of the Minimum, showing the action, the reason and the NASA source for each. It also includes a 7-day irrigation deficit planner, a Crop Doctor for plant symptoms, and Nova, an AI voice and chat assistant.
This answers the Field Shift challenge by helping farmers adapt as shifting monsoon cycles make droughts, crop failures and pest outbreaks harder to predict. Advice comes in English, Bengali, Hindi, Spanish and Swahili, can be read aloud, and works offline as a PWA, so it reaches farmers with limited literacy or patchy connectivity. By making satellite science simple, transparent and local, AgroNova helps protect yields, save water and strengthen food security.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

AgroNova is a climate-adaptation companion for smallholder farmers. As monsoon cycles shift, farmers face failed seasons, sudden droughts and unexpected pest outbreaks, while the NASA data that could help them is hard to read. AgroNova turns that data into simple daily decisions. A farmer picks a field on a map, and AgroNova reads NASA POWER, SMAP, GPM IMERG, MODIS/VIIRS, SRTM and FIRMS data for that location.

HOW IT WORKS

- Rotation Lab: ranks three crop plans (Water-Saver, Climate Resilience, High Yield) using Liebig's Law of the Minimum. Every result shows the action, the reason and the NASA source. Scores are deterministic code, not AI, so the same field and data always give the same ranking.

- Irrigation planner: combines NASA POWER readings with Open-Meteo forecasts and reference evapotranspiration to calculate a 7-day irrigation deficit.

- Crop Doctor: checks plant symptoms from a farmer's description or photo and suggests prevention steps.

- Nova: an AI voice and chat agronomist powered by Google Gemini, which writes advice in the farmer's language. If the AI is unavailable, a built-in rule-based advisor answers instead.

- Risk alerts: heat, spray-wind and fungal-risk advice from daily NASA POWER data, and FIRMS fire detection near the field.

NASA DATA (HONEST STATUS)

NASA POWER is used live. SMAP soil moisture, GPM rainfall, MODIS/VIIRS vegetation and SRTM elevation use dated demo samples for the demo field, and are clearly labelled that way in the app and our README.

BENEFITS AND INTENDED IMPACT

AgroNova helps farmers protect yields, save water and prepare for climate shocks without needing to understand satellite science. Advice comes in English, Bengali, Hindi, Spanish and Swahili, can be read aloud for farmers who prefer listening, and works offline as a PWA for areas with patchy internet.

TOOLS AND TECHNOLOGY

TypeScript, TanStack Start and Router, React 19, Tailwind CSS v4, Recharts, Leaflet with OpenStreetMap, Supabase, Drizzle ORM, Nitro and Vite, deployed on Vercel. Data and APIs: NASA POWER, Open-Meteo (ECMWF IFS), OpenFarm and Google Gemini. No special hardware is needed, only a phone or browser.

WHAT MAKES IT CREATIVE

We combined several NASA datasets into one decision instead of a dashboard of charts. Every recommendation is explainable and traceable to its NASA source. We pair deterministic science with AI, so AI explains the advice but never decides crop rankings.

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED

Language and literacy barriers, unreliable connectivity, transparency about which data is live and which is sample data, farmer privacy (photos are uploaded only if the farmer chooses), and graceful fallback when AI is unavailable.

WHAT WE WOULD BUILD NEXT

Replace the dated demo samples with live SMAP, GPM and MODIS feeds, add more crops and regional soil data, and pilot AgroNova with local farmers and agricultural extension workers.
dataRefs: NASA SMAP (L3 Enhanced Passive Soil Moisture)
